newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB says Tractebel-Powerfin merger open question.
newsitem.headline: SGB says Tractebel-Powerfin merger open question.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ste Generale de Belgique declined to clarify on Tuesday whether or not it will merge its Tractebel and Powerfin units once its public offer on Tractebel shares ends on October 30.

"We believe that the practical and common sense way to deal with the possibility of a merger between Tractebel and Powerfin is at the end of the price maintenance operation on Tractebel's shares," SGB chairman Etienne Davignon told a news conference on SGB's first half 1996 results. "Only then would we know what figures we are talking about."

SGB, which is loaded with debt after paying 49 billion francs for a 24.47 percent stake in Tractebel owned by rival Belgian holding Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, does not want Tractebel shareholders to take up its 14,500 francs-a-share offer.
As a means to discourage the shareholders from acting, it plans to distribute a put warrant, enabling them to sell under the same conditions in three years time.
"If we had thought that Tractebel would not be worth 14,500 francs in three years, we would not have bought it," Davignon said, commenting on the public offer.
Davignon said details of the offer would be published in the coming days. The prospectus for the offer has already been approved by Belgium's bourse watchdog, the Banking and Finance Commission.
SGB is 62 percent owned by France's Cie. de Suez.
